nodes.name: Carbon cloth pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A 1 × 1 cm² CC was ultrasonicated in acetone solution for 5 min, then rinsed several times with deionized (DI) water, and dried in an oven at 60°C for 1 h. After drying, the CC was immersed in a mixed solution of concentrated sulfuric acid and nitric acid with a volume ratio of 3:1 at room temperature for 12 h. After soaking, the CC was washed several times with DI water to remove the remaining acids. Finally, it was put into a 60°C oven to dry and set aside for further use.

nodes.name: FeCoNiLaPd electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: FeCl₂ (6.38 mg), CoCl₂ (6.49 mg), NiCl₂ (6.48 mg), LaCl₃ (12.26 mg), PdCl₂ (8.87 mg), and (C₂H₅)₄N(PF₆) (5.50 mg) were mixed and added to the organic solution consisting of CH₃CN (60 mL), CH₃CH₂OH (20 mL), and HCON(CH₃)₂ (20 mL). After the mixture was sufficiently stirred, electrodeposition experiments were conducted using pretreated CC as working electrode, titanium mesh as counter electrode, and Hg/HgO as reference electrode. The electrodeposition was performed at constant voltage of 3.0 V for 30 min under stable stirring at room temperature. After deposition, the working electrode was washed several times with ethanol and DI water to obtain the final FeCoNiLaPd HEA catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiLaPd shows distinct alloy phase peaks at 40.1°, 46.1°, and 68.2° attributed to (111), (200), and (220) facets with absence of individual metal patterns.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b presents the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the FeCoNiLaPd material with distinct alloy phase peaks at 40.1, 46.1, and 68.2° attributed to the (111), (200), and (220) facets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiLaPd has atomic percentages of Fe (18.8%), Co (22.6%), Ni (19.2%), La (31.2%), and Pd (8.2%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The quantitative analysis of inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) shows that the atomic percentages of Fe, Co, Ni, La, and Pd metals in FeCoNiLaPd are 18.8, 22.6, 19.2, 31.2, and 8.2%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiLaPd shows numerous ordered microsized spherical aggregations densely distributed on CC fibers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphological characteristics of the sample were examined by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), as illustrated in Figure 1d and Figure S3, which reveals the presence of numerous ordered microsized spherical aggregations.

properties.description: High-magnification image showing nanostructured surface with densely packed spherical nanoparticles forming clusters and aggregates

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiLaPd shows well-defined lattice parameter of 0.262 nm for (111) facet confirming crystalline alloy structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A detailed structural investigation of the HEA material was carried out using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), as depicted in Figure 1e,f and Figure S4. The well-defined lattice parameter of 0.262 nm for the (111) facet confirms the crystalline alloy structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiLaPd has average spherical particle size of about 200 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic force microscopy (AFM) image indicates that the average spherical particle size of FeCoNiLaPd is about 200 nm (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of FeCoNiLaPd reveals Co0 (777.1/792.3 eV), Co2+ (782.6/797.9 eV), Co3+ (780.7/796.8 eV) with higher Co2+/Co3+ ratio than FeCoNiPd; Fe0 (706.4 eV), Fe2+ (710.4 eV), Fe3+ (712.4 eV) with higher Fe2+; higher Ni0 with no Ni3+; Pd0 (335.2/340.6 eV), Pd2+ shifted to lower binding energies; La3+ present.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2a, the XPS Co 2p spectra reveal the presence of three distinct valence states, Co0 Co2+ and Co3+. ... the XPS La 3d spectrum of FeCoNiLaPd shows a considerable amount of the oxidized La species (La3+).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiLaPd HEA has larger specific surface area and smaller average pore size than FeCoNiPd, showing mesoporous feature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HEA materials show a considerable specific surface area and a unique mesoporous feature (Figure S1 and Table S1). Compared with FeCoNiPd, FeCoNiLaPd HEA has a larger specific surface area and smaller average pore size.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of FeCoNiLaPd during OER shows increasing peaks at 450 and 525 cm⁻¹ ascribed to eg-bonding and Alg stretching of Ni(FeCo)OOH species indicating surface reconstruction to metal hydroxyl oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 6a, the intensities of Raman peaks at 450 and 525 cm⁻¹ respectively ascribed to the eg-bonding vibration and Alg stretching vibrational bonding of Ni(FeCo)OOH species increase with the applied potential.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ DRIFTS of FeCoNiLaPd during OER shows peaks at 3250, 1650, and 1210 cm⁻¹ for *OH, H-O-H stretching and *OOH bending vibrations confirming metal hydroxyl oxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, in situ DRIFTS peaks with voltage increasing from 1.25 to 2.15 V are visibly observed at 3250, 1650, and 1210 cm⁻¹ ascribed to the stretching vibration of *OH and H-O-H species and the bending vibration of *OOH, respectively.
